Over the last four games, all wins, Illinois beat Michigan State in an overtime thriller, realistically knocked Oregon out of the College Football Playoff, handed Maryland its sixth loss, and gave Nebraska its fourth straight loss. Husker offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen was fired the next day – it wasn't the Illini's fault, but the loss didn't help. But now it's really on. It gets a shot to hand UCLA its first loss of the season this week, could ruin Iowa's College Football Playoff hopes next week, and might prevent Northwestern from finishing the regular season with a winning record to close. Meanwhile, all UCLA is doing is beating everyone. It joins Utah as the only two unbeaten teams left in college football, and with a win here, ho hum, it'll be 10-0 and, barring something insane, will be in the College Football Playoff. Illinois vs UCLA: Quick Hits This is the only trip outside of Illinois for the Illini in November. It finishes the home slate up against Iowa next week, and closes up the road at Northwestern. UCLA makes a trip to Michigan after this before finishing up down the road at USC. The two teams haven't played since the Illini beat the Bruins 20-14 in the 2011 Kraft Fight Hunger Bowl. The two teams are 6-6, starting the series with a 45-14 Illinois win in the 1947 Rose Bowl. It's not getting flagged, but penalties haven't been a problem this year. It's also not turning the ball over, but the offense has only given it up six times all season. No, it's really this simple – Illinois is scoring more points than the other teams. Yeah, ha ha, very funny, but there's just no other way to put it. All of a sudden, Illinois is just not giving up as many points. It's not like the defense has been a rock in the red zone, and it's still giving up plenty of yards. However, what it is doing is getting to the quarterback more, with eight sacks over the last four games after coming up with three in the first five. But … Why UCLA Will Win UCLA is just fine in low scoring, slugfest games. But as it showed last week against Minnesota, it now has an explosive element to its attack. The formula keeps on working. Hang around, don't screw up, keep the score low, and then drop the hammer and close like Mariano Rivera, pounding with the running game and owning the fourth quarter. But last week, the passing game ripped it up with the first 300-yard game of the season on just eight completions. Quarterback Ty Dieffenbach threw two 75-yard touchdown passes to Aidan Mizell, and he threw a scoring pass to Noah Fox-Flores. Minnesota dared Dieffenbach to throw well, and he did. Illinois vs UCLA Prediction, Betting Lines Illinois was able to survive an Oregon team that ran well, and moved the ball well, mainly because it didn't allow touchdowns and the Duck kicking game was a disaster. Other than that, for the most part, the Illini win when they keep the other side from pounding away with the ground attack. But the big problem for Illinois is an offense that can come up with big pass plays. The Illini are 0-3 when giving up more than eight yards per pass, and after last week, UCLA averages 8.4 yards per throw. Denver designated the second-year wideout for return early in the week on Wednesday, but a few good days of practice were enough to make it official. 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 13, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC Wake Forest is rolling toward the ACC title game. But SMU, which has never lost a home ACC game, can stay in the race. Time and date: Saturday, November 14 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-1.5) Over/under: 61.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 3-1 Last meeting: Wake Forest 13, SMU 12 — October 25, 2025 Current streak: Wake Forest, 1 (2025) Setting the scene This might be the ACC regular season game of the year. For the first time in College Football Playoff history, the ACC champion is guaranteed an automatic bid. Thus, just getting access to Charlotte keeps the door ajar for Wake Forest and SMU in this high-stakes conference showdown. The Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in college football, winning six consecutive games, primarily in blowout fashion. But the Mustangs haven’t ever lost an matchup at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, faring 12-0 in their previous contests. A Wake Forest win propels the Demon Deacons to the doorstep of the ACC Championship Game. An SMU win creates chaos, bringing a cluster of 2-loss teams back into championship consideration, including itself. The ACC races greatly hinges on what unfolds Saturday afternoon on The Hilltop. Wake Forest Demon Deacons outlook Wake Forest (8-1, 5-1 ACC) is ranked No. 13 by the College Football Playoff committee, situated as the second-highest ACC team. Since its lone September loss to Miami (FL), the Demon Deacons have been as dominant as anyone in the FBS. During the last five games of its six-game win streak, Wake Forest has defeated opponents by an aggregate score of 264-31, or an average of 53-6 per game. The Demon Deacons used a dominant defense to stun SMU 13-12 in last year’s meeting in Winston-Salem, but this season, the offense has hit its stride under second-year coordinator Rob Ezell. Wake Forest ranks fourth nationally in scoring (43.3 points per game), ninth in total offense, and 10th in passing. Starting quarterback Gio Lopez missed last week’s game against FCS Merrimack with a lower body injury, but the absence was permissible due to the level of opponent. The former South Alabama and North Carolina gunslinger has been phenomenal in his new home, delivering 18 touchdowns against one interception this year, ranking 13th nationally in passing average. His mobility has made defenses pay too, accumulating 317 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season. Lopez’s top target Carlos Hernandez is receiving national recognition. The senior is sixth in the FBS with an average of 105 receiving yards per game, and he regularly strikes from distance. Hernandez has multiple 70-yard touchdowns this season, and he has four outings with at least 110 yards and an end zone appearance. Jack Foley, Kam Shanks, and Antonio Meeks have provided support in this dynamic aerial attack, and the diversity in options allows Wake Forest to have the nation’s ninth-most efficient third down offense. The run game has been serviceable, ranking 43rd nationally in yards per game, while producing 4.94 yards per carry. Ty Clark and Deuce Lawrence have split carries throughout the season, totaling 416 and 327 rushing yards, respectively. Wake Forest’s offensive improvement has somewhat obscured the consistent impact of its defense. The Demon Deacons have only surrendered multiple scores once in their past five games, and they’ve finished 22 consecutive quarters without allowing more than seven points. The result is the country’s 13th-ranked scoring defense and 24th-ranked total defense — a unit which is particularly stingent against the run, surrendering just 85 yards per game on a 2.69 average. Defensive end Langston Hardy is the leader of the run-stuffing effort. He leads all ACC players with 13.5 tackles for loss, while also producing 44 tackles and 5.5 sacks. Backfield pressure has been a signature of this Wake Forest defense, and two other defensive linemen — Gabe Kirschke and Zach Lohavichan — have at least 7.5 tackles for loss. Wake Forest’s defense found the sustainable method of success, and that’s getting stops. The Demon Deacons are fifth nationally in both red zone defense and fourth down defense, finding ways to get off the field in critical situations. The unit can become even more dangerous if it dabbles in the turnover game. Wake Forest has forced just seven takeaways all season, which is tied for the eighth-fewest in the FBS. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (7-2, 5-2 ACC) prepares for a revenge game against Wake Forest. Had the Mustangs prevailed last October in Winston-Salem, they would have competed in the ACC Championship Game with a College Football Playoff spot on the line. Instead, they fell in a 13-12 heartbreaker on a last-second field goal — one of the program’s four ACC losses since joining the conference in 2024. Zero of those losses transpired at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. SMU has been a different beast at home, and that was evident in its most complete game of the season last Friday against Virginia Tech. Counting games against FBS opponents, the Mustangs registered a season-high 23 first half points, utilizing its strongest start of the season to push past the Hokies, 51-28. The concept of senior day might have lost some luster in the transfer portal era, but Saturday will feature one of the most emotional senior day moments in recent memory. Kevin Jennings is in his fifth year with the program and third as the starting quarterback, and the Dallas area native has poured a lot into the program. Jennings guided the Mustangs to an American Conference title, an ACC Championship Game appearance, a College Football Playoff berth, and a Holiday Bowl victory. Now he’ll play his final game in Dallas, entering the pivotal matchup fifth nationally with 2,764 passing yards and fourth with 25 touchdown passes. The most remarkable part of Jennings’ eye-popping stats is his efficiency. For a quarterback that slings it deep quite often, the senior boasts a 73.9 completion rate, which is second among all players with at least 100 attempts. Jennings has also limited interceptions this year, finishing four of his last five starts without one. SMU’s high-powered passing attack involves a slew of receivers. Yamir Knight, coming off a 103-yard, 3-touchdown performance, is the most frequented with a team-high 50 catches. But Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale are also heavily involved — especially on downfield attempts — and all three average over 15.0 yards per reception this season. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrström are also regular targets, tied for second on the team with four touchdown receptions apiece. The Mustangs’ run game is statistically a middle-of-the-road unit, ranked 70th in yards per game and 66th in rushing average. Kendrick Raphael operates as the top option, and he’s scored in seven of nine contests this year. Freshman Christian Rhodes has seen an increasing number of reps since mid-October, and he’s coming off a career-high 92 rushing yards against Virginia Tech. On defense, SMU displays a similar identity to the previous Mustang defenses of the Rhett Lashlee era: defensive line dominance. The Mustangs are one of 17 programs racking up at least 3.0 sacks per game, and defensive end Marques White is the ringleader of the movement. The eighth-year senior notched his third multi-sack game of the season last week, contributing to the turnover battle with a forced fumble and fumble recovery on the same play. But unlike the previous two seasons, SMU isn’t collecting turnovers on a consistent basis. The Mustangs have forced just eight turnovers all year, recovering five fumbles and picking off two passes. Despite the lack of takeaways, the secondary has shown considerable improvement from 2025, skyrocketing from 135th to 42nd in passing yards allowed per game, with safeties Jimmy Wyrick and Sael Reyes playing significant roles in that progress. Last year’s matchup between SMU and Wake Forest was the ultimate defensive battle. Just two touchdowns were scored — one on a 14-play drive and another capping a 41-yard series. There were eight combined turnovers in the matchup, which was decided on Connor Calvert’s 50-yard field goal as time expired. This year’s rematch looks bound to lean more on the higher-scoring end. Wake Forest brings significantly more offensive firepower in this matchup, headlined by the strong connection between Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons’ offense has been virtually unstoppable since the start of October, and while SMU should provide some resistance with a formidable defensive line, Wake Forest will still get its points in Dallas. However, SMU can thrive in a shootout style game. The Mustangs are one of the most explosive offenses in the country, ranking ninth in the FBS with 15 plays spanning 40 yards. Wake Forest has excelled at preventing the big play this year, but the Mustangs’ receiving corps should present challenges on the back end that the Demon Deacons haven’t seen since the Miami (FL) loss. This back-and-forth thriller will come down to crunch time. With the backing of its home crowd, SMU improves to 13-0 in ACC matchups at Gerald J. Ford Stadium — a result which will add significant chaos to the final two weeks of ACC play. In their latest action back on Saturday versus Merrimack, Wake Forest didn’t have any troubles. The Deacons scored four touchdowns in the second quarter alone and went to the locker room with a 49-0 edge. Wake Forest kept it going after that and eventually powered out a dominant 77-0 victory. picks.headline: Can Tennessee football keep pace in CFP race at Texas A&M? Our pick
picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football keep pace in CFP race at Texas A&M? Our pick - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong unanimously wins NL MVP TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Can Tennessee football keep pace in CFP race at Texas A&M? Our pick Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tennessee football 's push for a College Football Playoff berth continues with a game against Texas A&M. No. 9 Tennessee (7-2, 5-2 SEC) plays at Texas A&M (4-5, 1-5) on Nov. 14 (3 p.m. ET, ESPN). It will be just the second-ever visit to College Station for the Vols , who lost at A&M in double overtime in 2016. The Vols are riding high after a 34-6 home win over Kentucky on Nov. 7, which bumped them up five spots in the CFP rankings to No. 8. The last time Tennessee had a major home win was on Oct. 17 against Alabama, but then it had a let-down the next week and lost at South Carolina . Can it avoid a similar fate this time? Here's what to know about the matchup. Tennessee offensive lineman Gage Ginther (78) warm-ups before a football game between Tennessee and Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., Nov. 7, 2026 (Angelina Alcantar/ News Sentinel) Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre (12) on the sidelines before a football game between Tennessee and Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., Nov. 7, 2026 (Angelina Alcantar/ News Sentinel) Tennessee coach Josh Heupel watches warm-ups before a football game between Tennessee and Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., Nov. 7, 2026 (Angelina Alcantar/ News Sentinel) Smokey XII before a football game between Tennessee and Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., Nov. 7, 2026 (Angelina Alcantar/ News Sentinel) Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop (18) warm-ups before a football game between Tennessee and Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., Nov. 7, 2026 (Angelina Alcantar/ News Sentinel) Tennessee athletic director Danny White on the sidelines before a football game between Tennessee and Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., Nov. 7, 2026 (Angelina Alcantar/ News Sentinel) Two Northrop T-38 Talon flyover before a football game between Tennessee and Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., Nov. 7, 2026 (Angelina Alcantar/ News Sentinel) Jon Gruden meets Smokey before Tennessee’s game against Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Nov. 7, 2026. (Brianna Paciorka/News Sentinel) A young Tennessee fan pets Smokey XII before a football game between Tennessee and Kentucky at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., Nov. 7, 2026 (Angelina Alcantar/ News Sentinel) 1 / 9 Tennessee football vs Kentucky, see our best photos | Exclusive Tennessee football vs Kentucky, see our best photos | Exclusive See the famous faces who attended Tennessee football games in 2026 A disappointing season for Texas A&M, Mike Elko The Aggies made last year's CFP and were in the SEC title race for much of the season before stumbling down the stretch. They entered the 2026 season with a No. 8 preseason ranking. This season has been a fall from grace for coach Mike Elko and the Aggies, who are fighting for bowl eligibility and currently tied for last place in the SEC. Their only league win this season was against Arkansas and last week's 17-9 loss to South Carolina was their only defeat by less than two scores. They've lost five of their last seven games overall. QB Marcel Reed has struggled in senior season It's been a tough senior season for quarterback Marcel Reed, who has been the focus of many Aggies' fans frustrations as the season has taken a downward slide. He has 1,641 passing yards with eight touchdowns and eight interceptions this season, all major steps back from last year. Texas A&M's offense is averaging 16 points per game in SEC play, worst in the league. The Aggies' defense is middle of the pack in the SEC in scoring (seventh) and yards (ninth), although it's tied for last in sacks. It's not like there isn't talent at Texas A&M, like top receiver and future NFL draft pick Mario Craver. There's a reason it had high expectations. But that hasn't translated to success on the field in 2026. Tennessee's run game has been elite, led by DeSean Bishop Tennessee's passing attack still ranks last in the SEC, and by this point in the season it's not realistically going to rise much. But its run game has only gotten better with every week and has a tendency to wear opponents down and pay off in the fourth quarter. The Vols lead the conference with 216 rushing yards per game, Late-season recognition has been piling up for Bishop. UT kicked off his Heisman Trophy campaign this week as he crossed the 1,000-yard threshold for the season and scored his 13th rushing touchdown. With 1,066 yards this year and 2,597 in his career, Bishop could contend for the UT single-season record 1,491 yards and the career record of 3,078 yards. It's an advantageous matchup against Texas A&M's rush defense, which is 11th in the league at 129.9 yards allowed per game. Tennessee vs Texas A&M score prediction Tennessee 30, Texas A&M 20: This is another chance for Tennessee to stumble on the road after an emotional win like it did at South Carolina, but that Gamecocks team is much more dangerous than this one at Texas A&M. The formula is simple for the Vols: avoid penalties and turnovers and hand the ball off to Bishop. That should be enough to get the job done. This one seems likely to stay close at the start but for Tennessee to pull away in the second half. Emmett Siegel covers Tennessee baseball for Knox News. picks.headline: Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M
picks.blurb: Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong unanimously wins NL MVP TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: T.J. Searcy #18 of the Texas A&M Aggies reacts in the second half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jay Arnold · SB Nation Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:06 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas A&M returns to Kyle Field for the first time in three weeks after two straight road losses, sandwiched by an idle week. The Aggies fell 17-9 to South Carolina last time out in a contest that saw Texas A&M accumulate over 450 yards of offense and fail to produce a touchdown. The Aggies will hope to rectify that this week in College Station as they welcome the #8 Tennessee Volunteers to town. The trenches are going to be extremely important if Texas A&M is going to steal a win this Saturday. Let's dive into what needs to happen up front for the Aggies to come out on top. Offensive Line COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: Marcel Reed #10 of the Texas A&M Aggies runs with the ball in the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Against South Carolina, Texas A&M moved the ball well. As mentioned above, the Aggies racked up over 450 yards of offense. Rueben Owens ripped off multiple explosive runs, and Texas A&M had 206 yards on the ground. Yet, zero touchdowns made the hope that would be rendered by the yardage a grand disappointment instead. Simply put, field goals do not win games. The Aggies have to be able to finish drives off to win games, and Texas A&M has failed to do so in three out of the four road contests this season. The Texas A&M offense has fared better at home for the most part, but frankly I don't expect that to continue against an absolutely elite Tennessee defense. The Vols rank second only to Georgia in scoring defense. Tennessee's passing defense is staunch, though the Aggies wouldn't likely be able to test them there either. The rushing defense isn't in the upper tier of the conference but is also solid. Most significantly, the Volunteers lead the country in sacks. Defensive end Tyree Weathersby has seven sacks this season. The Vols also get pressure from the interior, as defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam has six sacks. Gilliam is a force to be reckoned with in the run game as well. I've thoroughly enjoyed watching film on the gifted DT this year, but I don't think his ability bodes well for this Texas A&M offensive line. I don't think this offensive line is horrible, and I think they've continued to play better as the season has progressed, but against this defensive front for Tennessee, it's going to feel like all that progress has left. In short, if the Aggies score a touchdown this week, I'd be surprised if it came from the offense. Defensive Line COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: Marco Jones #10 of the Texas A&M Aggies plays against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the situation for the offensive side of the ball is dire, I think the defensive side of the ball largely shouldered the burden well against South Carolina. The Aggies held what was the top rushing offense in the country at the time to under 100 yards right up until LaNorris Sellers ripped off a big run at the end. The Aggies also sacked Sellers twice, including a massive strip sack by Bryce Perry-Wright. We'll see if those run game improvements carry over as the Aggies face yet another powerful rushing attack. Powered by the legs of running back DeSean Bishop, Tennessee is the current top rushing attack in the SEC. However, if Texas A&M can find a way to slow down this rushing attack, the Aggies just might have a chance in this one. Discipline and sure tackling are going to be of the utmost importance as this Josh Heupel offense looks to spread opposing defenses out in order to capitalize on seams. Missed tackles against this Tennessee offense are extremely disastrous, and the Aggies can't afford to lose one-on-ones. The front four must maintain gap discipline as the secondary will be forced to honor Tennessee's formations. Get Tennessee behind the chains, and this becomes a drastically different ball game. While Tennessee ranks at the top of the conference in rushing, the Volunteers are the only team in the SEC below Texas A&M in passing offense. After Faizon Brandon started the season under center for Tennessee, George MacIntyre has since taken over. However, neither QB is a game changer on this offense, making the Vols basically one-dimensional. The equation for success against Tennessee is simple. Stop running backs DeSean Bishop and Daune Morris or get ground to a pulp. If the Aggies can make the improvements against the run permanent, they can hang around in this one – and that starts with the defensive tackle position and Brandon Davis-Swain, DJ Hicks, CJ Mims, and Landon Rink, in my opinion. While I think the Aggies keep this contest close in the first half, I think repeated three-and-outs by the Aggie offense eventually allow the Volunteers to wear down the Texas A&M defense in the second half. I have Tennessee winning this one 20-3. #BTHOtennessee

Published: Nov 12, 2026 · 10:00 AM EST The Tennessee Volunteers have come up with 2 of the most impressive wins of the season in the FBS, a 26-10 point pounding of Alabama and last weekend's 34-6 drubbing of Kentucky . Both teams were in the top 6 of the initial College Football Playoff Rankings. But despite the Vols being 7-2 with those 2 victories, and despite Tennessee's 2 losses each coming by a field goal against teams currently in the top 20 of those rankings, the Vols probably have to win out to make the field of 12. The Fearless Prediction knows how difficult it can be to win on the road in the SEC but will readily accept the challenge to make the correct call in Saturday's Tennessee- Texas A&M game. This will only be the second time that the Vols have made a trip to College Station. Back in 2016, they lost at Texas A&M in double overtime, 45-38, in a game best remembered for Tennessee RB Alvin Kamara's dominating performance. He had 18 carries for 127 yards and 2 TDs to go with 8 catches for 161 yards and a TD. It was the only game in Kamara's 2 seasons in Knoxville in which he was the focal point of the UT offense. If that doesn't summarize the missed opportunities of the Butch Jones era, nothing will. Fast forwarding to today, Tennessee's offense might not have a Kamara, but it does have a Bishop. The Vols' senior RB, DeSean Bishop, already has 1,066 rushing yards this season, and now stands 426 yards away from breaking Dylan Sampson's single-season rushing record of 1,491 rushing yards. Bishop (and Tennessee's offensive line) gets better as the game continues, and that certainly helps the cause with youth at QB. Redshirt freshman George MacIntyre completed 9-of-14 passes for 125 yards against UK, but more importantly he didn't throw an interception and he didn't fumble. But Josh Heupel added a wrinkle to the QB position, with true freshman Faizon Brandon (remember him?) seeing his first action since being pulled in the Auburn game a month ago. Brandon only took a couple of snaps. One in a single wing formation that resulted in a 29-yard run, and one a beautifully designed play in which Brandon tossed the football approximately 5 centimeters forward to Mike Matthews for what counts as a 24-yard TD pass. Heupel has now given opposing defensive coordinators more reason for concern the rest of the season, not knowing what else Heupel will come up with that Brandon package. Defensively, Tennessee continues to impress. It kept Kentucky out of the end zone for 60 minutes. It sacked UK QB Kenny Minchey 4 times while forcing 3 turnovers against a team that rarely coughed up the football. Tennessee is tied for 10th nationally in scoring defense (allowing 15.1 points per game), 18th in total defense (296.4 yards per game), and leads the nation in sacks with 39. LB Arion Carter is tops on the Vols in tackles with 59. DT Xavier Gilliam has a team-best 11.5 tackles for loss. As for Texas A&M, a season that began with so much promise has devolved into depression. The Aggies have lost 5 of their last 7 games, including a 17-9 defeat at South Carolina last weekend. They are 1-5 in SEC play. Mike Elko , now in his 3rd year as Texas A&M's head coach, has stuck with QB Marcel Reed, despite middling results. Reed throws for 182.3 yards per game, but his TD-to-INT ratio of 8:8 is not ideal. Rueben Owens II and K.J. Edwards combine to average 96.2 rushing yards per game. Mario Craver and Isaiah Horton are Reed's best options in the passing game, combining for 62 catches, 703 yards and 6 scores this season. Overall, the Aggies are only ranked 91st in the FBS in total offense, with 359.2 yards per game. The Aggies' defense will be a challenge for the Vols. ETSU and Tulsa transfer LB Ray Coney leads the team with 46 tackles. As a unit, they allow 320 yards per game, good enough to be ranked 28th nationally, while allowing only 18.7 points per game, 22nd in the FBS. Next week the Vols welcome Lane Kiffin and LSU back to Neyland Stadium. The Fearless Prediction will have a lot to say about that soon, but we aren't looking ahead. Tennessee better not either. And it won't. Kyle Field might be a tough place to play… but a lot of teams do win there. You'll be able to add Tennessee to that list. away.blurb: Wednesday night, the SEC released the initial availability report. Weathersby joins six players already out for the season. Texas A&M lists offensive lineman Trovon Baugh as doubtful and wide receiver Mario Craver as questionable. Craver is the Aggies’ second-leading receiver with 311 yards and three touchdowns. Below is the full availability report for Texas A&M. Saturday, No. 8 Tennessee will take on Texas A&M on the road in College Station, Texas. The Vols are coming off their big win over the Kentucky Wildcats last Saturday. In that game, edge rusher Tyree Weathersby went down with a season-ending knee injury. Tennessee had stayed fairly healthy for a while after the first few weeks of the season. Weathersby was having an amazing season as the sacks leader on the team and third in the Southeastern Conference with seven. Weathersby also had 20 tackles, two fumble recoveries and even a pass deflection this season. “I hate it for Tyree,” head coach Josh Heupel said Monday. “He’s played extremely well. He’s worked extremely hard. He was playing his best football. And I know he’ll bounce back from it, but obviously a huge bump in the road for him.” During Saturday’s win, tight end DaSaahn Brame exited the game after failing to maintain control of a pass in the end zone, according to the officials. Brame’s head hit the ground hard, and he was eventually helped off the field. He is not on the report, and Heupel said on Monday’s “Mike Keith Show” that he should be good to go. Heupel also spoke to the incomplete call. “DaSaahn’s doing good. We feel like he’ll be in a great spot for game day. When I was talking with the officials, we hadn’t gotten the report back postgame yet. That typically happens in the middle of the week. “But at the end of the day, he didn’t come down with the football, didn’t maintain control of it when he was on the ground. So that was the ruling that they gave me, and they said that they did review it up top as well.” No. 8 Tennessee and Texas A&M will kick off at 3 p.m. ET Saturday at Kyle Field in College Station, Texas. The game will be televised on ESPN. The Vols will try for their first win at Kyle Field after losing in double-overtime, 45-38, during their only other visit there back in 2016. home.headline: 2 key Texas A&M wide receivers' statuses remain unknown
home.blurb: Knowing that Marcel Reed will continue to start, combined with Holmon Wiggins calling plays, the Aggies need every wide receiver available not just for development, but to provide the passing game a spark and help produce more touchdowns. Texas A&M (4-5, 1-5 SEC) once again failed to hold a late lead during last Saturday's 17-9 road loss to South Carolina, as the Aggies couldn't reach the end zone for the third time in SEC play, matching the 1971 Texas A&M offense that did not score a touchdown in three conference games. After racking up over 450 yards of offense against the Gamecocks , it's baffling how starting quarterback Marcel Reed has regressed to this level, while first-year offensive coordinator Holmon Wiggins will reportedly retain his position for the rest of the season, based on coach Mike Elko's comments during Monday's press conference. As miserable as the season has been, injuries have hurt the passing game, especially over the last two games, as junior wide receiver Ashton Bethel-Roman and sophomore wideout Kelshaun Johnson missed the South Carolina game, forcing freshman Aaron Gregory to play more snaps. Marcel Reed has struggled in the passing game throughout the season, but played his best game against the Gamecocks, completing 25/43 passes for 251 yards, and should have thrown a touchdown to transfer wide receiver Isaiah Horton, who dropped at least three passes that would have resulted in six points or kept drives alive. Elko did not provide an injury update for Ashton Bethel-Roman or Kelshaun Johnson, which isn't a great sign heading into Saturday's home test vs. No. 13 Tennessee. "No, no updates on those guys." But the Hoosiers, who have yet to announce a starting quarterback for the game, can calm the waters by notching a quality win over the visiting Trojans. USC is lagging outside the CFP picture…for now. That will change if the Trojans can upset IU on the road after beating Ohio State in their last game during Week 9. A win would also catapult USC into the Big Ten title race, revitalizing a season that appeared to be in peril after a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin on Oct. 24. The question is which Indiana quarterback the Trojans will be tasked with defending. Season-long starter Josh Hoover injured his throwing arm during Indiana's Week 9 win over Minnesota and was benched after subsequent struggles. Veteran backup Grant Wilson entered and completed 9 of 17 passes for 156 yards and a touchdown, sparking a quarterback controversy. Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti was noncommittal this week on who will take the first snaps for IU, forcing USC to be ready for either option. The situation has created some late-season intrigue for the reigning national champions, who have been unable to pull away from most of their Big Ten opponents during an 8-1 (5-1 Big Ten) start. USC vs. Indiana: Need to know Can USC match Indiana's physicality?: Regardless of who is at quarterback for Indiana, USC's defense will have its hands full with the Hoosiers' skill talent. Physical receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh comprise one of the best 1-2 tandems in college football. Meanwhile, IU running backs Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr . are both averaging more than five yards per carry and are over 700 yards each for the season. USC has never been known for its physicality under coach Lincoln Riley, but keeping the Hoosiers in check will require it. Going on the road and winning against a team with Indiana's gritty DNA wouldn't just be a huge boost for the Trojans' playoff aspirations; it would also help change the perception of Riley's program. Indiana's CFP outlook: Indiana's chances of making the playoff will reach near "lock" status at 96.2% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. A loss would leave the Hoosiers with a 66.8% chance of selection and bring greater scrutiny to a resume lacking high-end fare. An Oct. 10 win over Nebraska is not aging well, as the Cornhuskers are on a four-game losing streak. After that, IU's best win is either on the road against a 5-4 Michigan team or at home against a 6-3 Northwestern team. However you slice it, the Hoosiers don't have a win against a team currently ranked in the CFP Top 25. Beating USC would change that...assuming the Trojans remain in the rankings. USC's CFP outlook: This is do-or-die for USC's playoff hopes. The Trojans' chances of making the field will rise to 51.5% with a win and plummet to 3.7% with a loss. In other words, the playoff has already started for Lincoln Riley's team. It's really a simple formula: finish 3-0 with wins over Indiana, Maryland and USC, and the Trojans will unquestionably make the playoff for the first time. Lose any of those games, and it's probably over for what is arguably the most historic program to have never appeared in the CFP. The only exception was a 47-15 win against an overmatched Rutgers team. The Hoosiers haven't shown the ability to pull away and dominate quality opposition. So long as IU limits catastrophic turnovers, it will win the game on the basis of its physicality on both lines of scrimmage. But it's difficult to envision the Hoosiers suddenly pulling away from a team of USC's caliber. The Trojans have a veteran quarterback in Jayden Maiava who can keep his team in the game. USC vs Indiana Prediction: Are the Trojans Really In the CFP Hunt?

Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:37 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just when it seemed like USC was finished, and a new era would soon start with Lincoln Riley all but gone after an ugly 24-7 loss at Wisconsin, a funny thing happened – the Trojans rolled Ohio State 30-18. And now, at 7-2, with high-profile dates remaining against CFP No. 9 Indiana and No. 8 UCLA, No. 18 USC all but controls its own path to the CFP – a 10-2 Trojan team with two top-ten wins in the final three games wouldn't be a lock to get in, but … yeah, it would be. But Indiana is still pretty good. It's 8-1, this close to being 9-0, and even though the schedule hasn't been a killer, if it keeps winning, all will be just fine. But lose this, and the pressure will be on to avoid a slip over the last two weeks. USC vs Indiana: Quick Hits Indiana travels to Washington after this before finishing with the rivalry date against Purdue. USC hosts Maryland after this before the showdown at UCLA. It's just the fifth meeting ever, and the first since USC joined the Big Ten. The Trojans are 4-0, including the 1968 Rose Bowl. How To Watch USC vs Indiana Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, IN – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – How many 3-loss CFP teams will there be? Why USC Will Win Plenty of things have to go right. USC has the punting to own the field position game, there can't be a slew of turnovers, and Indiana has to keep struggling. The only way to put it is that it's like the Hoosiers forgot how to score. The offense is moving a bit, but it hasn't scored more than 20 points in regulation since early October. The USC passing game continues to be good enough. The ground game might be hit-or-miss, but Jayden Maiava is a smart, tough veteran who keeps hitting his throws for the Big Ten's best offense on third downs. Why Indiana Will Win Indiana got a week off to reset at just the right time. No, it's not playing nearly as well offensively as it did last year. No, it doesn't have that dominant mode, and it certainly doesn't have the same passing game. And yet it's still 8-1 – this bunch finds ways to win. For all of the issues on offense, the defense continues to be outstanding. The run D is the fourth-best in the nation, allowing just 2.3 yards per carry overall with no touchdowns in the last three games. USC might throw well, but it wasn't all that long ago that the ground game was stuffed for -18 yards by Wisconsin. USC vs Indiana Prediction, Betting Lines Is Grant Wilson up to the gig, or will Josh Hoover get the nod as he fights through an injury? No matter who ends up under center, he'll be fine against a USC defense that's been hit hard by injuries. Indiana's offense – even without banged up star RB Turbo Richard – will be a bit more effective than it was against Ohio State, Michigan, or Minnesota, but it'll be the defensive front and run defense that keeps the good season going. picks.blurb: Former Notre Dame head coach picks USC to beat Indiana - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong unanimously wins NL MVP TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Former Notre Dame head coach picks USC to beat Indiana Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As USC football prepares for a season-defining game at Indiana , one very interesting plot twist has emerged: A former Notre Dame head coach picked the Trojans to beat Curt Cignetti and the Hoosiers. Brian Kelly, now a commentator for CBS Sports, knows what it's like to coach in the state of Indiana. He recently said on air that Lincoln Riley's Trojans will go into Bloomington and win. This is not an earth-shaking story which possesses overwhelming significance, but it's a story worth noting because it's so fascinating on multiple levels. Brian Kelly had the upper hand over and against USC in most of the years he coached Notre Dame. Why is he trusting USC now? Notre Dame and Indiana fans had a very spirited argument before and after the Fighting Irish 's victory over the Hoosiers in the 2024 College Football Playoff. Notre Dame finished as the 2024 runner-up. 2025 Indiana, under Curt Cignetti, went one step beyond the Irish and won the national championship. Brian Kelly has no real reason to pick games for any reason other than he sincerely thinks one team will beat the other, but it's notable that he would trust USC and distrust Indiana. Both schools' fan bases don't like Notre Dame. It is simply interesting to wonder why Kelly is pivoting to the Trojans and away from the Hoosiers. Is there any underlying emotional reality which might have nudged Kelly in the direction of USC? Let's keep in mind that Kelly wants to return to coaching. Is his USC pick in any way motivated by how he sees the coaching carousel or the national landscape? We'll never know the answers, but the questions are legitimately interesting. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan Wolverines suffered one of the worst losses in modern program history on Saturday, falling at home to the Michigan State Spartans, who came into the game sitting at 2-6 and on a six-game losing streak, 15-6. I've floated the phrase "rock bottom" around a couple of times this year, but this is it. We've hit rock bottom, and now the Wolverines have to go on the road to take on the Oregon Ducks. Last week, I predicted Michigan was going to lose to Michigan State because I didn't think that Kyle Whittingham was going to get his team motivated for a rivalry game. The Spartans are a bad football team, but they clearly have a coach who is trying and who cares. Sure enough, both teams embodied their head coach in that game. Michigan was lifeless, unenthusiasic, and just flat out looked like a team that didn't want to be there. After the game, Michigan fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, which needed to be done. However, nothing will change until the Wolverines find a new head coach who embraces the program and actually wants to do his job. With a road test against a ranked team looming, things are only going to get worse. Here are a few predictions for this weekend's contest against the Ducks: Michigan will get shut out We almost saw this happen last week at home against one of the worst teams in the Big Ten, so why should we expect a better performance out west against the Ducks? Players have checked out and the head coach doesn't want to be here. The recipe going into this game could not be worse. Before the Michigan State game, things were bad, but a win would've made the Wolverines 6-3. And the losses, while painful and self-inflicted, were somewhat forgivable. However, there is no coming back from the atrocity we witnessed last weekend. It will only get worse. Kyle Whittingham will be fired after the game The one positive that will come from last week's disaster is that I can't see any scenario where Whittingham is Michigan's head coach on Dec. 1. The fan base is now completely against him, and the program is at its lowest point in over a decade. It's going to happen within the next month, and I think Saturday might be so bad that the school decides to get it over with before the end of the season. Oregon wins 17-0 I think that the defense will once again do enough to put Michigan in a spot to win a football game, but the offense isn't going to get it done. It will be another frustrating watch, but we will move one step closer to putting this dumpster fire of a season in the rearview mirror.

The Oregon Ducks are in a good spot as the team enters the upcoming week of the college football season. Despite the Ducks having three losses on their resume, Oregon remains very much alive in the hunt for the College Football Playoff. In the new rankings for the playoff , Oregon came in ranked at No. 16, giving this team a real chance to get in. After taking down the Ohio State Buckeyes a week ago on the road, Oregon has put itself in a strong position to make some history. No team in the history of the playoff has reached the bracket with three losses, but this could be the year for it to happen. However, the Ducks will still need to win out for this to become any form of reality, and the team has three games left. First up for Oregon is a matchup at home against the Michigan Wolverines this weekend, with the Ducks feeling very confident heading into the game. Related stories With how the teams have played of late, Oregon is seen as the favorite to take down Michigan, giving this group more of a chance for the playoff. But the Ducks can't overlook the Wolverines, especially with their margin of error being so slim for the rest of the way. Bleacher Report's David Kenyon predicted the games of the week, including this matchup between Oregon and Michigan. In the prediction, Kenyon has the Ducks taking care of business against the Wolverines by a score of 28-13. Oregon starting quarterback Dante Moore is out for the rest of the year due to injury, and it's the Dylan Raiola show now. Raiola has given the Ducks some hope this season, providing a spark on offense. Raiola has thrown for 1,354 yards with 11 touchdowns and two interceptions in seven games played for the Ducks this year. Losing Moore hurt this team, but Raiola has brought a sense of calm to the entire offense, giving them a chance to make some history. Against Michigan, Raiola will be called upon again, with him needing to put together a strong showing. The Wolverines can be a tricky team, with freshman quarterback Tommy Carr expected to get the start again this week. Carr has shown some ability to handle college defenses, but the Ducks can't take him lightly. If Oregon can take down Michigan, it would bring them that much closer to a playoff appearance.

home.headline: Oregon's Teitum Tuioti exits Ohio State game with injury. What we know
home.blurb: Coach Dan Lanning said Nov. 9 Tuioti will be out for the rest of the season. The 6-foot-3, 263-pound senior out of Sheldon High School is the Ducks' third-leading tackler this season with 44. He also has a team-high 9.0 TFLs and eight quarterback hits. His 5.5 sacks are second on the team. Tuioti's injury came on a fourth-and-13 pass rush with 9:16 to play as his leg buckled when he was attempting to spin out of a block. COLUMBUS, Ohio – Oregon pulled off the upset Nov. 7 with a 41-28 win against Ohio State. But the victory came with a costly injury for the Ducks . Starting outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti injured his knee in the fourth quarter and was wearing a wrap as he was carted to the locker room after the game ended. "Unfortunately, Teitum's done for the year," Lanning said. "He had a knee injury, he'll end up having surgery. He's going to have to wait a little bit for things to settle down. I hate it for him, because it's kind of a routine, weird play that it happened on." In 51 career games, Tuioti has 200 tackles, 36.5 TFLs and 22.5 sacks. He was a three-year starter who does have one more season of eligibility remaining at Oregon, though a he also projected to be a Day 2 NFL Draft pick. "I don't know if he'll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is going to be really really lucky," Lanning said. "Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year and every year that he's been here. Watching him grow as a player and as a person has been really fun for us." Teitum Tuioti injury: How it happened He was down on the field for a few minutes and needed help getting to the sideline. Tuioti had two tackles in the game, including one for a loss of yards. He also played a key role in one of the Ducks' most impactful plays when he took a direct snap with Oregon in punt formation and threw a 30-yard pass to fellow outside linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei for a first down. picks.headline: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line
picks.blurb: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong unanimously wins NL MVP TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Sam Hutchens, Mississippi Clarion Ledger · The Clarion Ledger Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads OXFORD − Ole Miss football must win on the road against Oklahoma to keep hopes of a College Football Playoff appearance alive. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). The Rebels are coming off a 42-7 home loss to No. 1 Georgia that put its CFP hopes on the edge of extinction. A viable path to the CFP begins with winning the final three games of the season. This is the third consecutive season Ole Miss has faced Oklahoma and the Rebels have won the first two matchups. Like Ole Miss, the Sooners made the College Football Playoff in 2025. OU returned quarterback John Mateer but has struggled to complement a strong defense with a steady offense. Although the Sooners have losses to Michigan, No. 1 Georgia, No. 13 Kentucky and No. 24 South Carolina, OU has beaten two teams that Ole Miss lost to in No. 8 Texas and Florida. Here are five predictions about the matchup, including the final score: Jason Witten will have new wrinkles for OU offense vs Ole Miss defense The matchup pits defensive coaches against each other in Ole Miss' Pete Golding and OU's Brent Venables. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten could be the wild card. The former Dallas Cowboys tight end was elevated to the interim offensive coordinator position after Oklahoma fired Ben Arbuckle. Five days after Arbuckle was dismissed, OU beat Florida 23-7 in a game where it had 351 total yards. The Oklahoma offense played clean, efficient football under Witten. The Sooners suddenly seem to have new life offensively, which comes at a bad time for an Ole Miss defense that was ravaged for 481 yards vs Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss, John Mateer both throw interceptions With three games remaining, Chambliss' interceptions have tripled this season. He threw three in a spectacular 2025 season, but is up to nine in 2026. Golding attributed the increase to a combination of bad reads, bad luck and bad throws. Chambliss has thrown at least one interception in seven games this season. That plays into the hands of Oklahoma, which is No. 4 in the SEC with nine interceptions. The Sooners are also No. 5 in the conference with 26 sacks. Chambliss has been more vulnerable when under pressure. OU quarterback John Mateer has had turnover problems as well. He's thrown seven interceptions and has two lost fumbles. Look for both defenses to come up with an interception. The Sooners' stingy defense is better prepared to recover from interceptions than Ole Miss. When OU picks off Chambliss, it will give the ball back to a Sooners' offense that looks well prepared to chew clock and limit the chances for the Rebels' offense. Ole Miss gives Makhi Frazier, Shekai Mills-Knight both at least 10 carries Even with a quarterback as capable as Chambliss, it will be hard for Ole Miss to attack Oklahoma through the air. OU has the No. 1 passing defense in the SEC (170.7 yards per game). OU is No. 7 in the SEC in rushing defense (122.6 yards per game), but it's the weaker of two stout options. Ole Miss needs running backs Shekai Mills-Knight and Makhi Frazier to play well. Those two players are the primary backs with Kewan Lacy ruled out with a shoulder injury. Mills-Knight and Frazier combined for 17 carries for 60 yards vs Georgia, but they should get more carries against Oklahoma. Oklahoma leads in time of possession, Ole Miss relies on big plays Opponents are 31-for-112 (27.7%) on third down conversions against the Sooners. That's the lowest mark in the SEC and No. 4 nationally. That indicates Ole Miss will have trouble maintaining long, slow-developing drives. The key to combat that is explosive plays. Ole Miss could use a big game from Deuce Alexander. The receiver leads Ole Miss with 669 receiving yards, but he was held without a catch against Georgia. He is Ole Miss' fastest, most explosive player and the primary threat to score a deep touchdown. Ole Miss is on the other end of the spectrum. The Rebels allow 44% of third down conversions, which is No. 14 in the SEC. The Sooners clinched the game against Florida with a 20-play march in the fourth quarter that consumed 12:45 on the clock. The Rebels must avoid that fate. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma score prediction Oklahoma 24, Ole Miss 23: This should be a close game that will be determined by whether Ole Miss' defense or Oklahoma's offense does better. Right now it feels like the OU offense has more momentum. The Rebels are more desperate, but feeling like you need to press and make big plays on the road against OU's defense is a bad place to be. away.headline: Kewan Lacy injury update, Ole Miss football RB out for season, per report
away.blurb: News Sports Business Entertainment Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals OLE MISS Kewan Lacy injury update, Ole Miss football RB out for season, per report Sam Hutchens Mississippi Clarion Ledger Updated Nov. 12, 2026, 11:13 a.m. CT Ole Miss football running back Kewan Lacy is expected to be out for the remainder of the 2026 season, according to a report from On3 on Nov. 12. Lacy had offseason surgery on his left shoulder following the 2025 season. It was initially injured earlier that season, when he broke out as one of the best running backs in the nation. Lacy can return to college football in 2027, but also has the opportunity to enter the 2027 NFL Draft. He is projected as one of the top running back prospects in the field. It is his first season being eligible to be drafted. Lacy, a junior from Dallas, has been dealing with nagging injuries since Week 1 of the regular season. He missed a Week 4 game at Florida with an injury to his left shoulder. After dislocating that same shoulder in Week 8 at Texas, Lacy missed the Week 9 game against Georgia. He also has played through a lower-body injury he sustained against Vanderbilt in Week 6. He has already been ruled when No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) plays at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). Ole Miss depth chart: Who replaces Kewan Lacy at RB? The running back rotation behind Lacy has started to be established. It will be a combination of Michigan State transfer Makhi Frazier and sophomore Shekai Mills-Knight. Mills-Knight has gotten the biggest increase in carries as the season has progressed. He has 33 carries for 165 yards and three touchdowns in 2026. His career-high in attempts (16) and rushing yards (71) came against Auburn on Oct. 31. He got 13 carries for 52 yards against Georgia on Nov. 7. Mills-Knight is a former four-star prospect in the 2025 recruiting class, according to the 247Sports Composite. LSU transfer JT Lindsey and Joshua Dye are in the mix, too. Dye is a transfer from Southern Utah who has earned praise from Ole Miss coach Pete Golding for his pass protection. Here are Lacy's stats from his six games in 2026. Injuries have prevented Lacy from repeating the stellar season he had in 2025, when he ran for 1,567 yards and a school-record 24 touchdowns. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. picks.headline: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh
picks.blurb: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong unanimously wins NL MVP TRENDING Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Poch's looming Man United move Skubal suitors emerge Story by Wildcats Wire Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 11, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football failed the first test of this important November stretch, losing 34-6 to Tennessee . The Wildcats have to get off the mat quickly as they host the Florida Gators on Saturday night at Kroger Field. This is a Florida team that is reeling as they have lost four of their last five games. We will preview both sides of the football for the Gators, but we will start with their offense which is led by their star running back. Running back Jadan Baugh is essentially the entire Gators offense, he is the engine that makes it go. Similar to what we said about Tennessee's DeSean Bishop, but the Gators have struggled recently to get this run game going. That is the main reason they have lost four of their last five games. When you look at the win/loss splits of Baugh's stat line, it tells the whole story of Florida's offense. In the Gators' five wins this season, Baugh has rushed for 691 yards on 108 attempts for 12 rushing touchdowns and is averaging over six yards per carry in those wins. He has averaged 138 rushing yards per game in those five wins. Conversely, in Florida's four losses this season, Baugh has rushed for 145 yards on 52 attempts for 2 rushing touchdowns and is averaging under three yards per carry. He is averaging just 36 rushing yards per game in those losses. Teams have started to key in on the run game and slow Baugh down recently, as most of his success came in the first month of the season. In September when the Gators were rolling, Baugh had 600 rushing yards on 83 attempts and 11 of his 14 rushing touchdowns came in the first month of the season. He was averaging 150 rushing yards per game and over seven yards per carry in the month of September. Since then, Baugh has just 236 rushing yards on 77 attempts, averaging just 47 rushing yards per game and three yards per carry. It is simple for Kentucky's defense, stop this rushing attack led by Baugh and you will be in a great position to win this football game. Florida has a quarterback issue, as they have flipped back and forth between Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones. Philo was efficient in the first month of the season, but he dealt with an injury that allowed Jones to start in a big win on the road against Texas. Philo returned against Georgia, but a couple of boneheaded mistakes sent him to the bench. Jones completed 22-of-35 pass attempts for 155 passing yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the win over the Longhorns. Against Georgia and Oklahoma, the Gators only scored a total of 15 points. In those two losses, Jones completed 28-of-47 passes for 305 passing yards and no touchdown passes to three interceptions. Jones has thrown just four touchdown passes on the season and five interceptions. Philo on the other hand, has completed 70% of his passes this season for 1,367 yards for nine passing touchdowns. Philo also has five interceptions on the season. The biggest issue has been the injury of wide receiver Vernell Brown, who has not played in a game since the win over Ole Miss in September. Florida is struggling to generate any offense outside of the run game. This matchup is simple for Kentucky, they just have to key in and stop the run game for the Gators. Force Florida into a dropback heavy game, which will lead to turnover opportunities. Regardless if they start Philo or Jones, both have been turnover prone this season and the Gators are -3 in the turnover margin which ranks 98th among FBS teams. Kentucky's defense has to get stops early and play with a lead quickly. This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh

Neither Kentucky nor Florida will feel good coming into this one. Kentucky dropped a stinker in Knoxville, losing 34-6, while Florida got whipped by Oklahoma in The Swamp, 23-7. But they’ll both have to get over it quickly; the SEC comes at you fast. Florida will travel up to Kentucky for a November night game; the last time that happened was just last year. Kentucky rolled to a 38-7 victory. But both coaches are different, and I am not so sure a blowout is in the cards this year for either side. Both teams will look to right the ship and prevent one loss from becoming two. You better believe Jon Sumrall and Brad White will be coming back to Lexington with a win on their minds, while Kentucky will be looking to take the awful sting of that Volunteer loss out of their system while also keeping their College Football Playoff hopes afloat. Florida Gators (5-4, 3-4) Florida is a shockingly inconsistent team. The Gators destroyed Ole Miss by 24, knocked off Texas by 3, but lost by 28 to Missouri and 16 to Oklahoma. The Gators have been held to under 10 points in back-to-back games while also playing a QB carousel. Trammel Jones started against the Sooners but was a dreadful 10-of-22 with 2 INTs. But just a game before, Aaron Philo started 5-of-7, but those two incompletions were interceptions, and he was benched before halftime. Where the Gators go from there is anyone’s guess, but Kentucky will need to prepare to see both guys. On defense, Florida is just as volatile. 425.3 total yards per game is what they give up for the year, but in the last 3 games, they have surrendered 278 yards to Texas, 318 to Georgia, and 351 to Oklahoma. So, Brad White has got his side playing a little better. But it really comes down to which team shows up. Will it be the team that knocked off Texas or the team that lost at home to Oklahoma? Kentucky and Florida are both coming off terrible losses, with both fan bases hurting. Whichever team handles that the best will walk away with a victory here. I think if Kentucky can get back to playing clean football, they have the talent and home-field advantage to send the Gators back home with a loss. But Florida has a lot of talent, and if they are motivated, they can beat anyone, anywhere, as proven down in Austin when they knocked off Texas. My biggest concern remains Malachi Wood, who has been abused by speed guys this season. Emmanuel Oyebadejo is a 6’6, 300-pound nightmare who leads the Gators with 4.5 sacks. You better believe he is licking his chops to go against the right side of Kentucky’s line, which struggled down in Knoxville. picks.headline: How No. 11 Kentucky football and Florida match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (69.9% completions, 1,979 yards, 14 touchdowns vs. two interceptions) had two uncharacteristic turnovers in UK’s disappointing 34-6 loss at Tennessee last Saturday. The 6-2, 211-pound, fourth-year player from Hendersonville, Tennessee, threw his first interception in seven games on a shot play into the end zone. Minchey also lost a fumble after being hit on a UT blitz. • Florida coach Jon Sumrall has not committed to a starting QB this week. Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo (70.5% completions, 1,367 yards, nine TDs, five picks) began the season as the UF starter but suffered a shoulder injury on his throwing arm (right) in Florida’s 38-19 loss to South Carolina on October 10. Philo returned in the Gators’ 27-8 loss to Georgia on Halloween, but was ineffective. Tramell Jones Jr . (65.8% completions, 712 yards, four TDs, five interceptions) led UF to its 27-24 road upset of then-No. 7 Texas on Oct. 17 but has thrown no touchdowns and three picks in the two games since. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • After carrying only once in Kentucky’s two previous games, UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (541 yards, 5.5 yards a carry, eight touchdowns) ran the ball 11 times for 54 yards and caught four passes for 19 yards in the loss at Tennessee. Redshirt senior Jovantae Barnes (272 yards, 5.4 yards a carry, one touchdown in six games) carried seven times for 48 yards at Tennessee but lost a costly fumble. Third-year player Jason Patterson (473 yards, 6.1 yards a carry, three TDs) had 30 yards rushing on seven carries in Knoxville and caught a pass for four yards. • Florida’s Jadan Baugh (836 yards, 5.2 yards a carry, 14 touchdowns) is one of the best backs in college football. However, after the 6-1, 225-pound junior from Atlanta ran for more than 130 yards in each of UF’s first four games, he has run for more than 60 yards only once in the past five contests. As a freshman in 2024, Baugh ran for 106 yards and five touchdowns vs. Kentucky in a 48-20 Gators’ win in Gainesville. Advantage : Florida Wide receivers • Kentucky’s Kenny Darby is tied for the team lead in receptions (45) and leads the Wildcats in receiving yards (576). The 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, caught seven passes for 69 yards in the loss at Tennessee. After missing UK’s win over Vanderbilt due to injury, senior Nic Anderson (20 receptions, 223 yards, one TD) returned at Tennessee and caught three passes for 26 yards. • At 6-3, Florida’s Dallas Wilson (35 catches, 465 yards, three TDs) gives the Gators a big target on the outside. Wilson caught four passes for 48 yards in UF’s 23-7 loss to Oklahoma last week. A transfer from Georgia Tech, Bailey Stockton (36 catches, 373 yards, three touchdowns) provides Florida a steady threat in the slot. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez (45 catches, 405 yards, three touchdowns) has caught multiple passes in all nine UK games to date and has had four receptions or more in seven. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School had one catch for eight yards in last season’s 38-7 Kentucky pummeling of Florida at Kroger Field. Mikkel Skinner (10 catches, 97 yards, one TD), a 6-4, 235-pound second-year player, has carried the ball seven times out of the backfield and caught three passes combined in Kentucky’s past three contests. • Florida’s Luke Harpring , another Gator transfer who followed offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner from Georgia Tech, has made 14 catches for 165 yards. Junior Amir Jackson has made his seven catches count: They have gone for 133 yards and a touchdown. Jackson had a 48-yard catch in UF’s 44-39 win at Auburn on Sept. 19. Offensive line • In the loss at Tennessee, the Kentucky offensive front surrendered four quarterback sacks, six QB hurries and eight tackles for loss. Nevertheless, ESPN analyst Cole Cubelic wrote that UK center Coleton Price , the 6-3, 308-pound transfer from Baylor, “showed up, (and) had a great game.” • Another transfer from Georgia Tech, Florida center Harrison Moore is the interior anchor of the Gators’ front. Left guard Knijeah Harris has started UF’s past 34 games. Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (32 tackles, six sacks, nine tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) made five stops, 1.5 TFL and had a sack at Tennessee. Tackle Tavion Gadson (29 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveres) had four tackles with a TFL vs. UT. • Florida sophomore edge Jayden Woods (37 tackles, 4.5 sacks) is disruptive. End Emmanuel Oyebadejo , a 6-6, 299-pound senior from Manchester, England, had 2.5 sacks in UF’s win at Auburn and has 4.5 on the season. Advantage : Even • Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey remains second in the SEC in tackles with 78. The 6-3, 240-pound fourth-year player made six stops at Tennessee. Godfrey had three stops, including a tackle for loss in UK’s win over Florida last season. WLB Bo Barnes (60 tackles, 3.5 TFL) made seven stops vs. UT. • Florida WLB Myles Graham , a 6-1, 228-pound, homegrown junior from Gainesville, leads Florida in tackles with 70 and has four sacks, five TFL, three QB hurries and two fumble recoveries. Graham had a season-high 15 tackles in last week’s loss to Oklahoma. MLB Aaron Chiles has made 52 tackles, broken up three passes and recovered a fumble. Defensive backs • Kentucky will start a pair of former Florida Gators in its secondary. Safety Jordan Castell is tied for the SEC lead in interceptions with four and is tied for sixth in the league with 68 tackles. Last year, playing for Florida, Castell made seven tackles vs. UK. Nickelback Aaron Gates , another ex-Gator, is tied for fifth in the SEC with seven passes defended. In last season’s win over Florida, safety Ty Bryant tied for the UK team lead with six. This year, the senior from Frederick Douglass High School is tied for the SEC lead with four picks and has made 68 tackles, broken up three passes and recovered a fumble. • Florida free safety DJ Coleman has made 39 tackles, intercepted two passes and broken up three. Right cornerback Ben Hanks III leads UF with four pass breakups. Even as the Florida secondary has struggled, former Kentucky safety Cam Dooley , who made 29 tackles and picked off a pass last season for UK, has played a minimal role and has made only two tackles so far this season. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui supplied all of UK’s points in the loss at Tennessee with field goals of 43 and 25 yards. On the season, Zouagui is 12 of 15 on field goals with a long make of 52 yards. Punter Wilson Berry averaged 37 yards on three kicks vs. UT, but twice pinned the Volunteers inside their 20-yard line. On the season, the Australian is averaging 42.7 yards and has stopped six of his 13 punts inside the opponents’ 20-yard line. • Florida punter Alec Clark , who formerly kicked for both Marshall and Tulane, is averaging 47.1 yards a kick and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line on 14 of 31 punts. Place-kicker Patrick Durkin is 11-of-12 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 53 yards. Punt returner Vernell Brown III returned two punts for touchdowns of 64 and 70 yards, respectively, in UF’s 52-3 pasting of Campbell on September 12 but has missed UF’s past five games with a knee injury. picks.headline: Florida vs. Kentucky predictions, picks, odds: Tuesday's lines for Week 11
picks.blurb: Florida enters the matchup unranked in both major polls with a 5-4 overall record and a 3-4 mark in conference play after its 23-7 loss to Oklahoma at home on Saturday. Kentucky, on the other hand, is 7-2 (5-2 SEC) and ranked 13th in both the US LBM Coaches Poll and AP Top 25 heading into the 11th week of the college football slate, but is also coming off a defeat of their own - a 34-6 beatdown by Tennessee in Knoxville this past weekend. The Gators hold a commanding lead in the all-time series, with a 55-22 record against the Wildcats dating back to 1917, plus a 22-13 mark in Lexington. However, UK won the battle at Kroger Field last year, 38-7, and has prevailed in four of the last five meetings with UF. Stream Florida vs. Kentucky with Fubo free trial Florida vs. Kentucky odds, money line, over/under Odds courtesy of BetMGM as of Tuesday, Nov. 10 Moneyline: +140 / -175 Spread: Kentucky by 3.5 Over/under: 53.5 Florida vs. Kentucky predictions, picks for college football The Gators are averaging just under 13 points in their four losses this season, with a 27-point effort against Texas sandwiched in the middle across the last five games. Just when the defense appeared to be figuring some things out, the offense has mysteriously gone AWOL. Perhaps part of the reason is the absence of Vernell Brown III, who has been out of action since his injury during the Ole Miss game, and also the futility of the running game, which had been among the most formidable in the country over the first four games of the season before evaporating before our eyes. Kentucky's defense has been decent this season, but nowhere near elite, ranking 44th overall in the SP+ ratings and 71st according to Pro Football Focus - which also ranks the run defense at 95th - so Florida's offense could potentially figure things out. Hope springs eternal, so we are counting on a change of fortune in Week 11 and an upset victory for the Orange and Blue. away.headline: Gators Announce Starting QB Ahead of Clash with No. 11 Kentucky
away.blurb: GAINESVILLE, Fla. — The Florida Gators are making yet another change at quarterback. Aaron Philo, who had been benched for last week’s loss to Oklahoma , will return as the starter for this week’s game at Kentucky. Gators Announce Starting QB Ahead of Clash with No. 11 Kentucky Skip to main content SI.COM CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz was first to report. The decision is the latest in a series of moves at the position between Philo and Tramell Jones Jr., as struggles at the position have mounted over the last month. Philo was replaced by Jones Jr. in losses to Missouri and South Carolina before missing the Texas game with an injury. Jones Jr. threw for two touchdowns in that start and replaced Philo after three drives, two weeks later in the loss to Georgia. Last week’s loss to the Sooners was a negative turning point for the true sophomore, though, with Jones Jr. completing just 10 of his 22 passes for 133 yards, no touchdowns, and two interceptions. He played all but one offensive snap, with Philo coming in for a handoff for just one play. “Think both guys have done some really good things this year at times, and both guys have done some not-so-good things at times,” head coach Jon Sumrall said on Monday. “Didn't think we played well enough at quarterback on Saturday.” Pick your champion (you can change it later). Florida’s recent struggles at the position — a microcosm of other issues on the offensive line, injury issues at receiver, and difficulties in the run game with the running backs — have led to outside discussions on the long-term status of the position and both Philo’s and Jones Jr.’s individual futures with the program. Offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said the team’s focus remains on developing those currently on the roster and not looking towards the NCAA Transfer Portal to address the position. “We got three games to evaluate everything,” he said. “Look, one thing about me is if I tell you, like, I do believe in them. And I do understand that it is a process with the quarterback position, and I will not rush that process, right? I want to stand by those guys. I'm gonna bring them along. It's our job to coach them.” Kickoff on Saturday between Florida and Kentucky is at 6:15 p.m., with television coverage on ESPN.
