home.headline: Gators Announce Starting QB Ahead of Clash with No. 11 Kentucky
home.blurb: GAINESVILLE, Fla. — The Florida Gators are making yet another change at quarterback. Aaron Philo, who had been benched for last week’s loss to Oklahoma , will return as the starter for this week’s game at Kentucky. Gators Announce Starting QB Ahead of Clash with No. 11 Kentucky Skip to main content SI.COM CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz was first to report. The decision is the latest in a series of moves at the position between Philo and Tramell Jones Jr., as struggles at the position have mounted over the last month. Philo was replaced by Jones Jr. in losses to Missouri and South Carolina before missing the Texas game with an injury. Jones Jr. threw for two touchdowns in that start and replaced Philo after three drives, two weeks later in the loss to Georgia. Last week’s loss to the Sooners was a negative turning point for the true sophomore, though, with Jones Jr. completing just 10 of his 22 passes for 133 yards, no touchdowns, and two interceptions. He played all but one offensive snap, with Philo coming in for a handoff for just one play. “Think both guys have done some really good things this year at times, and both guys have done some not-so-good things at times,” head coach Jon Sumrall said on Monday. “Didn't think we played well enough at quarterback on Saturday.” Pick your champion (you can change it later). home.headline: Final availability report: No. 13 Tennessee vs. No. 6 Kentucky
home.blurb: Head coach Josh Heupel’s team has remained pretty healthy since the early-season injury problems. In this week’s availability reports, the Vols listed no new names and look to have everyone available. Earlier in the week, Heupel was asked how managing a team in November is different than September, and if they are equipped for it. On Friday night’s report , Kentucky reported four players out: inside linebacker Antwan Smith, inside linebacker Justyn Hartley, defensive back Jaden Smith, and defensive back Grant Grayton. Antwan Smith, Jaden Smith, and Grant Grayton have been out for quite some time. Outside linebacker Sam Greene and defensive back Isaiah McMillian were listed as probable. McMillian was initially questionable on Wednesday night but made progress. They are both removed from Saturday's report and available. Xavier Gilliam tunes out the hype as No. 13 Tennessee prepares for No. 6 Kentucky No. 13 Tennessee and No. 6 Kentucky will kick off at 6:20 p.m. ET at Neyland Stadium. The Vols lead the all-time series with 86 wins, 26 losses and 9 ties, and carry a five-game win streak against the Wildcats into Saturday night. “I think you’re constantly trying to improve," Heupel said. "You’ve heard me say it, good teams continue to get better every part of the season. Every week’s its own season, too. And so you’ve got to be great in your preparation, how you practice, put yourself in a position to play smart football. Certainly as you go through the year, injuries, where you’re at, all those things, you have to manage it really week by week. Tends to be more towards the end of the season. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Louisville vs. North Carolina in Week 11
picks.blurb: Louisville football is riding a four-game win streak, as the Cardinals sit in third place in the ACC and face maybe their toughest ACC opponent during this streak. The Cardinals travel to a gritty North Carolina squad, which sits 5-4 on the season, including 2-3 in conference play. Louisville football vs. North Carolina early odds and a prediction However, the record doesn’t tell the full story about this UNC season, as Bill Belichick and his Tar Heels have played much better football this year. They played Notre Dame and Miami very closely earlier this season, and their two ACC wins are over 6-3 Pitt and 7-2 Duke. With Louisville trying to punch their ticket to the ACC Championship Game, the Cardinals' showdown against the Tar Heels this weekend is massive. So, with the weekend quickly approaching, we wanted to make some bold predictions for this crucial ACC matchup. Isaac Brown bounces back with 100+ rushing yards We predict Isaac Brown will have another breakout performance. The star running back had just 38 rushing yards on seven carries in the Cardinals' win, but if Louisville wants to win on the road, Brown must have one of his dominant performances. In three of the Tar Heel’s four losses, an opposing running back rushed for 120 yards or more, including two games where the opposing running back earned at least 130 rushing yards. Brown as had a dominant second half of the season, rushing for 100 yards or more in three of his last five games, and we think a recipe to defeat UNC is through their star running back. We predict Isaac Brown will score at least one touchdown and rush for at least 100 yards for the fourth time this season. Louisvilles sacks the QB at least three times A major key to winning this matchup on Saturday is Louisville getting to the Tar Heels' quarterback, Billy Edwards. The Tar Heels have struggled to protect their QB at times this season, giving up three sacks to TCU, Pitt, and Clemson; two sacks to Duke and Syracuse; and a whopping four sacks to Miami. Louisville’s defensive line must put pressure on Edwards, and we think they will. We predict Clev Lubin and this defensive line will get to the quarterback for at least three sacks. The Cards are coming off a dominant performance against Georgia Tech, where they sacked the QB four times, and have sacked the QB at least twice in seven of their nine games and have sacked the QB at least three times in five games, including three of the last four. Lincoln Kienholz throws for 275+ Lincoln Kienholz has been one of the Cardinals' best players this year, and he continues that on Saturday. The 4-star transfer has thrown for 2,276 yards and 14 touchdowns this season, and on Saturday, we expect Kienholz to post at least 300 total yards again. Kienholz is one of the best dual-threat QBs in college football, and he showed that last week. Kienholz led the Cards to their fourth straight win, rushing for 81 yards and throwing for 182. He has thrown just three interceptions this season, and in a crucial road matchup, we think he will lead the Cards to a victory. We predict Kienholz to throw for at least 275 yards and rush for at least 50 yards. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The Wildcats will try to spoil the Utes' perfect season in a ranked battle Big 12 battle Getty Images Utah's trip to Arizona in Week 11 wasn't circled on many schedules before the 2026 college football season began, but the Big 12 matchup is a showdown between ranked teams and has serious College Football Playoff implications. The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number. (Photo by Patrick Mulligan/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brian Pedersen · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Twice this season, Arizona has found itself up against a ranked opponent with a chance to make a big splash on the national stage, and both times it led at halftime only to fall in the end. Third time's a charm? No. 22 Arizona (7-2, 4-2) plays its biggest game of the year on Saturday, hosting unbeaten No. 2 Utah (9-0, 6-0) with a chance to climb back into the Big 12 title race and the hunt for a College Football Playoff spot. How will the Wildcats do in this Top 25 clash? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Utah wins 30-28 Utah is not a team that has difficulty scoring. The Utes average 34.3 points per game against their FBS opponents this season. Their lowest output was 21 points against Houston. They've only been held below 30 points by three of their FBS opponents: Houston, BYU, and (surprisingly) Colorado. Arizona will be Utah's third ranked opponent but first on the road. Will it matter that the game isn't in Salt Lake City? Doubtful. The Wildcats had issues with mobile quarterbacks. While Arizona is ranked fifth in the Big 12 with 203.3 pashing yards allowed per game, Devon Dampier doesn't just rely on his arm to move the ball. He throws for 228.1 ypg. He's also second on the team in rushing with 53.6 ypg on the ground. Dampier is going to be playing in his home state against his former head coach. The now-assistant coach at Arizona admits that he should have played Dampier more when they were both at New Mexico. The senior from Phoenix may have something to prove and a group of friends and family members in attendance to prove it to. On the positive side, Arizona should be able to move the ball, too. Utah is ninth in the Big 12 in passing yards allowed at 233.8 per game. Noah Fifita is fourth in the nation in passing yards per game (310.4), total passing yards (2,794), and total offense per game (325.4). The Arizona defense has been solid for most of the year, but it barely kept the Big 12's 15 th -ranked scoring offense under 30 points last week. Utah is the No. 2 scoring offense in the league. The Wildcats are No. 6. To make matters worse for the 'Cats, Utah has the No. 2 scoring defense in the Big 12. Arizona's in No. 5. With some luck, this one could be close. It would be a shocker to see Arizona pull off the upset, though. Ezra Amacher — Utah wins 27-24 Utah's Devon Dampier is the type of quarterback that gives Arizona defensive coordinator Danny Gonzales cold sweats at night. The senior from Saguaro High School in Phoenix has grown into one of top dual-threat quarterbacks in the country. He ranks second among all active FBS quarterbacks with 2,811 career rushing yards. He has a dang good arm as well and doesn't commit many turnovers. Arizona struggled to stop the other dual-threat QBs it faced this year in TCU's Jaden Craig and West Virginia's Michael Hawkins Jr. Dampier is better than either of them and has a stalwart offensive line protecting him. I don't see the Wildcats defense being able to do enough to keep Utah off the board. That wouldn't be as much of a concern against a lesser opponent, but Utah's defense is outstanding. The Utes give up 16.3 points per game, second-fewest in the Big 12. They're riding high on confidence after forcing BYU's Bear Bachmeier into four interceptions last week. I give Utah the edge. Adam Green — Arizona wins 31 -27 Why the hell not. Here in this space is where I try to convince you all (and myself, really) that this pick is an actual prediction rather than wischasting. So here we go. Arizona is good — very good — at home. Utah has not beaten a ranked team on the road. Arizona has everything to play for and is coming off a victory that likely served as a wake up call while inspiring confidence. Utah, on the other hand, has a little bit of breathing room and is coming off an emotional and physical victory over rival BYU. Finally, Arizona has Noah Fifita . The QB is a perfect 2-0 against Morgan Scalley's defense, with the most recent victory coming in Salt Lake City during a season in which the Wildcats were not a particularly good team. That Fifita is playing the best football of his career heading into this game and has weapons like Isaiah Mizell and Giovanni Richardson is nothing to feel bad about. This isn't to say that it will be an easy game like the last time these teams played in Tucson, because it's hard to imagine No. 2 in the nation going down without a fight. Utah's offense is going to be more dynamic than we're used to seeing but their defense is gettable for an Arizona team that is quite capable of slinging the ball around. Keep penalties to a minimum and win the turnover battle, and Arizona will win the game. Juan Serrano — Arizona wins 31-28 Arizona is a different team when it plays inside Casino Del Sol Stadium. Of course, last week's game was a miracle and not usually how the Wildcats play at home. The defense did only surrendered 21 points to TCU which is usually a winning formula. Noah Fifita 's pick-six was a rarity and kept the Horned Frogs in the game. He cannot afford to have those type of plays against Utah, and I don't think he will. Fifita usually has some of his best games against the Utes. I also think Arizona missed two shots at a big win against BYU and Texas Tech. It's time for the ball to bounce in the way of the Wildcats in terms of making a statement. Utah has only been favored by 2.5 since the end of the Holy War, and it has stuck there. That is a very good sign for Arizona. Devon Dampier does present a big issue for the defense but I would not be surprised if Danny Gonzales presents a different picture for Dampier. He knows his defense has struggled against mobile quarterbacks and it has shown in many games. Something will need to change schematically for the Wildcats to have a chance to win. It all comes down to what is at stake for Arizona. This is a season defining, program defining moment for Brent Brennan 's squad. The home winning streak will continue for the Wildcats and will earn one of the most historic wins in Arizona football history. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 30-24 I'm not going to lie, I've been tossing this one back and forth in my mind. The Wildcats at home are a force to be reckoned with. I throw out the issues from Arizona last week as kind of fluky. They were coming off an emotional loss against Texas Tech, and on a short week no less. Noah Fifita's rare and odd pick six, Dwight Bootle's rough night and the not-great tackling were all things that caused the closeness of the game against TCU. On the other side, you have Utah coming off an physical and emotional Holy War win against BYU last week. As of this writing, Utah looks like they'll be without their leader in sacks, DL Karson Kaufusi , who has 3 sacks this year. However, the Utes still have Jireh Moe and Elijah Elliss , who are also fantastic d-linemen and have combined for 62 tackles, 9.5 TFLs and 5 sacks. Overall, this game is going to come down to QB play. Not breaking any news here, but Noah is a stud and will have to play a near flawless game. If he plays his game and doesn't force anything, or make any plays like last week's pick six, Arizona has a legit chance to win. For the Utes, Devon Dampier is a problem. He has been effective through the air this season, however, his legs are his biggest strength. He is a fantastic runner and is Utah's second leading rusher. Even if he doesn't gain massive yards, he is able to extend plays and forces the defense to respect his running ability. Finally, I think Danny Gonzales will change some things up for Utah. I don't expect to see the same looks that TCU got, mainly due to the injuries on defense. I believe Danny has learned from the Tommy Castellanos issues and won't make it as easy for Dampier. Couple that with slowing down Wayshawn Parker and playing in front of what seems to be turning into a packed Sol, I think the defense can do it. Brian Pedersen — Arizona wins 21-20 As I wrote earlier this week , November has traditionally been the month when Arizona has picked up its biggest home wins. It's been a while, though, and most of those have been when the Wildcats are a decided underdog and the game isn't in the national spotlight. Not the case this time, with a very small spread and Fox's Big Noon Kickoff is in town. The losses at BYU and Texas Tech had a common theme beyond leading at halftime. Both saw the UA struggle mightily in the second half, scoring only nine total points, though each time it was down four and driving with a chance to go back in front. One missed play turned everything. Utah is a very good team with no weakness, and has the kind of dual-threat weapon in Devon Dampier that Arizona traditionally struggles with. But it's November, and strange things happen at night in the desert. picks.blurb: Utah Utes expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm November 13, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football During their decade-plus together in the Pac-12, Arizona and Utah had plenty of great battles, but the results tended to be streaky. The Wildcats won four straight meetings from 2012-15, then Utah took six in a row before the UA claimed the last two, including their Big 12 debut in 2024 when it beat a Top 10 Utes squad on the road. But the opponent coming to Tucson this weekend is better than any of those previous versions. Utah is 9-0 and ranked No. 2 nationally, one of two unbeaten teams in FBS. To better understand the Utes, we reached out to Josh Furlong of KSL.com for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his spirited answers to our lifeless questions: AZ Desert Swarm: What have been the main keys to Utah getting off to its best start since 2008? Josh Furlong: “The easy answer is quarterback Devon Dampier, who has been healthy and efficient as the team’s biggest playmaker, but it ultimately comes down to the culture Morgan Scalley has built at Utah in such a short time. He’s allowing the players to be loose while focused, understanding that it takes each person to contribute to wins. He’s an extremely competitive coach, but he’s able to pair that with a system that allows players to make mistakes, grow and develop.” Arizona fans still have nightmares about Devon Dampier from two years ago at New Mexico, and he seems to have only gotten better. Where has his game most improved this season, and is there anything he still struggles with? “Dampier has worked on going through his progressions and staying in the pocket more, which has allowed Utah to do more with him at QB. It’s giving him more structure while understanding that he still needs room to freelance and be the dynamic QB he can be. All of that has allowed him to have more confidence, especially now that he’s been paired with a better group of wide receivers. At times, though, he gets happy feet and doesn’t have the right mechanics in his throws, which can sometimes limit his passing.” Wayshawn Parker apparently got banged up against BYU but should be good to go for this game. What does he bring to the offense when healthy? “Wayshawn Parker simply opens up the options for Utah’s offense. His threat as a runner, especially as he breaks through tackles, makes him one of the top offensive names you have to take away. But by doing so, opposing defenses have to handle many other players that can be just as effective in advancing the offense — Dampier, Daniel Bray, Byrd Ficklin, Braden Pegan, Creed Whittemore, etc. On top of that, he’s really developed a great pass blocking game, which has been a huge advantage in keeping Dampier upright and doing what he does.” Arizona’s secondary has been dealing with injuries and got exploited a bit last week with deep passes. Who would be the beneficiaries of this in the Ute receiving corps? “The primary receiving target would be Braden Pegan (WR1), who is a multi-faceted receiver who can do pretty much anything needed, and is paired with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore. Johnson is a smooth runner with great separation and great hands. Whittemore works primarily in the slot and has been great in the intermediate game, especially with opposing defenses focusing on Pegan and the potential run threats of Dampier, Ficklin, Parker. Another option is tight end Noah Bennee, who is the benefactor of all the other skills players being the top of mind. As the defense focuses on other players, Bennee sneaks out and can be a problem with his size.” How do you expect Utah to defend Arizona’s passing attack? “Utah will primarily operate in man coverage and force Noah Fifita to beat them one-on-one, while the defensive coordinator Colton Swan schemes up disguises and blitzes to keep Fifita uncomfortable. Because Fifita is so explosive, it’s likely Utah will try more contain while pressuring him.” Morgan Scalley had been the coach in waiting at Utah for a while, and we’re seeing why with this 9-0 start. What are the biggest differences between him and Kyle Whittingham? “The biggest difference is that Scalley is a people’s person. Kyle Whittingham cared more about coaching football and not the other elements, whereas Scalley sees it all interconnected. He shares the same hard-nosed, physical approach of Whittingham but wants a connected team that has no factions. It’s not, offense gets to know offense and defense gets to know defense, it’s a team-wide look as each works to understand the other. He’s also open to feedback, assuming that the feedback actually is presented in a way that helps change and it’s just complaining, though he’d listen to anyone who is frustrated. He wants all to feel connected and bought into the program, regardless of their standing with the team.” Prediction time. Does Utah move one step closer to an unbeaten regular season or does Arizona pull off a November upset at home and stay in the hunt for the Big 12 title game and the playoffs? Give us a score pick. “This game in Tucson is always a tricky one. Even when Utah has been the clear favorite, it’s far from a decisive win for the Utes. I think Scalley has his squad more focused on this game than it might have been in year’s past, which leads me to believe Utah will be ready for any blow and not be caught off guard in a road environment. I think Utah is the more complete team, but they’ve got to stop Fifita. To me, Utah wins this game if they can contain Fifita (as much as possible) and cannot give up momentum to an opposing crowd. I see Utah winning something like 31-24 .” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. However, Friday’s update was the bearer of bad news for Colorado fans. All but one of those players were ruled out, and the final member of that list’s status is still undetermined. The Longhorns have recovered from a few early miscues and jumped back into the SEC title race. The Longhorns have won three straight games, including a 34-20 win over No. 18 Missouri last week. LSU faced its biggest test of the season against No. 5 Alabama and faltered, losing 31-13. The Tigers were unable to find any offensive consistency in the loss, rushing for only 2.3 yards per carry as the Crimson Tide won in all three phases. Texas and LSU have only played 18 times in history, and not in Baton Rouge since 1953. The last time they played was in 2019, when legendary quarterback Joe Burrow threw a dramatic touchdown pass on third-and-17 to put the game away. This is also their first-ever matchup as conference mates. Texas vs. LSU: Need to know Arch settling down: Texas quarterback Arch Manning had some growing pains midseason, especially with inconsistent performances against Florida and Oklahoma . But over the last two weeks, the former No. 1 overall recruit has come into his own. The junior is completing 76% of his passes with six touchdowns and zero interceptions over the last two wins. Top defenses: Statistically, Texas and LSU are two of the top three defenses in the SEC, joining Georgia in nearly every relevant category. The Tigers are better against the run, holding opponents to 2.7 yards per carry. Texas is especially good against the pass, holding opponents to 5.4 yards per pass attempt with eight touchdowns to six interceptions. Expect a low-scoring battle in Death Valley. Major CFP implications: Texas remains in solid shape for the postseason, even with a third loss, because of their strong resume. LSU, though? The Tigers' dreams are almost completely dead. They are 0-3 against ranked opponents and ranked outside of the top 20 in the CFP Rankings. The only saving grace is that they have games remaining against the No. 6 Longhorns and No. 8 Volunteers -- and frankly, that might not even be enough at 9-3. picks.headline: Brian Kelly Makes Bold Prediction for LSU-Texas Week 11 Showdown
picks.blurb: Brian Kelly Makes Bold Prediction for LSU-Texas Week 11 Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS A pair of SEC blue blood contenders face off under the lights, each playing in seemingly different directions, and with serious postseason implications for both. LSU has split its last two games, is coming off an ugly loss to Alabama, and is outside the playoff bubble. Texas is on a three-game win streak, has defeated two ranked SEC opponents, and is the No. 6 team in the bracket. Looking at the matchup, Brian Kelly sees this going one way, and for one reason. Brian Kelly projects LSU-Texas matchup “I think in this game, one can be fixed and the other can’t. And that is, I don’t know if Texas can protect. I don’t think you can fix that over a week,” Kelly said on CBS Sports. "I don't know if Texas can protect. I don't think you can fix that over a week." @CoachBrianKelly is going with @LSUFootball over the Horns this weekend 👀 pic.twitter.com/9fap1Zx4aH “For LSU, it’s situational football. They have to be better in the red zone. They have to be better in fourth down situations. I think you can correct situational football with execution. I don’t know if [the Longhorns] can protect. I’m going with LSU.” Longhorns have struggled at the line Winning games and getting better play from Arch Manning has lifted much of the negative attention around Texas at a critical point of the season. But what happens in the trenches could decide who prevails in Death Valley, and on paper that matchup may not go the Longhorns’ way. Coming into this weekend, Texas has allowed 27 sacks of Manning. That number accounts for the ninth-most of any team in college football this year. Moreover, issues with blocking have conspired against their rushing offense. Texas is averaging a meager 128 yards per game on the ground. That ranks 108th in the country and 14th in the SEC. LSU is currently projected as being 0.9 points better than Texas on the same field, according to the ESPN Football Power Index prediction model. Texas is a perfect 4-0 against top 25 ranked teams this season and playing for its playoff life. LSU is just 2-2 and looking to get back in the conversation. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Predicts Texas Falls at LSU in Major College Football Playoff Shake-Up Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy believes No. 21 LSU has the one weapon capable of derailing No. 6 Texas on Saturday night, and he’s backing Lane Kiffin’s Tigers to protect Tiger Stadium against Arch Manning and the Longhorns. On his Always College Football Week 11 preview , McElroy picked LSU to win 24-20 and called the Tigers’ pass rush against Texas’ protection “probably the most lopsided matchup on the board” on a slate with four games between ranked playoff teams. Why does McElroy trust LSU? Louisiana State Tigers defensive end Princewill Umanmielen (1) looks on during the second quarter against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The former Alabama quarterback built his pick around one mismatch in the trenches. “LSU has one of the best pass rushes in the country, and Texas has one of the shakiest pass protections,” McElroy said. The former Alabama quarterback built his pick around one mismatch in the trenches. “LSU has one of the best pass rushes in the country, and Texas has one of the shakiest pass protections,” McElroy said. Texas (7-2) is coming off a 34-20 win at Missouri in which Manning threw for 297 yards and three touchdowns, but he still went down three times. McElroy pointed to the quarterback’s patience as part of the problem. “He does hold the ball looking for the perfect throw, and behind that line, the perfect throw sometimes arrives after the defense arrives,” McElroy said. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, an Austin native who followed Kiffin from Ole Miss, is the player McElroy expects to attack a Texas line that has struggled with twists and stunts. The Longhorns also listed offensive lineman Trevor Goosby as out on their availability report for the Missouri game. McElroy said three LSU sacks would leave Texas “in third-and-long, where it converts just 20% of the time.” Sam Leavitt and LSU’s red zone LSU Tigers Quarterback Sam Leavitt | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect LSU (6-3) brings flaws of its own after a 31-13 home loss to Alabama. LSU (6-3) brings flaws of its own after a 31-13 home loss to Alabama. Sam Leavitt completed 35 of 47 passes for 380 yards, but the Tigers went 0-for-4 on fourth down and scored one touchdown on four red zone trips. “I wouldn’t think that would equal 13 points ,” Kiffin said afterward. Alabama’s fourth-quarter surge in Baton Rouge led Booger McFarland to declare the Crimson Tide a playoff lock , and Texas brings a defense built to repeat that formula. The Longhorns rank first nationally in adjusted defensive EPA per play, according to Game on Paper . “Texas’ defense is good enough to hold LSU to field goals, which is why I think this stays a fight,” McElroy said. LSU’s tempo is the Tigers’ counter. McElroy noted that LSU runs nearly 80 plays per game and said, “If LSU’s tempo has the Texas linebackers gassed by, say, the fourth quarter, then the best defense on the field stops being the best defense on the field.” What’s at stake in Baton Rouge? McElroy said a fourth loss would make LSU’s playoff chances “a no-go,” while a win would put the Tigers “back in the playoff mix.” The New Orleans native grew up attending LSU games, but Steve Sarkisian doesn’t expect the homecoming to distract his quarterback. “I don’t think he gives a crap, I’ll be honest with you,” Sarkisian said. “I really think he’s thinking about what coverages they’re going to play .” Kiffin, who recruited Manning at Ole Miss, offered praise with one exception. “I think he’s an awesome kid and I hope he does really well, obviously outside of Saturday,” Kiffin said. LSU linebacker Whit Weeks, who fractured his right fibula against Texas A&M on Sept. 26, was listed as doubtful against Alabama. McElroy said a Weeks return against Texas would be “enormous for the LSU defense.” Texas and LSU kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. LSU and Texas are set to meet in Baton Rouge this weekend in a matchup that could officially eliminate the Tigers from the College Football Playoff conversation. With three losses, LSU's playoff hopes are already on life support. A fourth loss would pull the plug. Texas, meanwhile, needs to win to avoid a third loss, which would put their playoff chances in jeopardy. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Texas vs LSU ESPN's Greg McElroy made his picks for this weekend's biggest college football games, and he has LSU winning a close one over Texas. LSU has a 25% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 3% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 8, 2026). "LSU runs more plays than anyone in the entire FBS — nearly 80 a game — and at a pace that doesn't let Texas substitute," said McElroy . "Texas is used to facing about 68 plays by the opposing offense. So, if LSU's tempo has the Texas linebackers gasped by the fourth quarter, and the best defense on the field stops being the best defense on the field, then [it's a positive for the Tigers]. "LSU's pass rush against Texas's protection is probably the most lopsided matchup on the board. It's happening at home at night. The Texas defense is good enough to hold LSU to field goals, which is why I think this stays a fight. But if Texas becomes one-dimensional, then an offense that has to throw against this (LSU) pass rush is going to spend way too much time off schedule behind the chains. I'm taking LSU to win this game 24-20 . At night in Death Valley, that's when that pass rush gets a sixth man, and I don't know if Texas's O-line can hold up throughout the night." Texas and LSU are set to kick off at 6:30 PM CT/7:30 PM ET. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. The Longhorns are 7-2 and No. 6 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. The Tigers are 6-3 and all the way down at No. 21. If Texas wins … boom. It will have eight victories, including great wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, and Missouri, to go along with two 27-24 losses to Florida and Oklahoma. Add a win at LSU to the résumé, and it keeps moving along, but losing one of its last two games to Arkansas or Texas A&M would make it a fight to get in, even with the great résumé of wins. If Texas wins, LSU is done. However, even at 6-3, things might get a bit interesting if LSU pulls this off. The three losses to No. 3 Alabama, No. 11 Kentucky, and No. 19 Ole Miss might end the debate, except for one key factor – next week, the Tigers play at No. 8 Tennessee. Close strong, hope for a slew of losses from other SEC teams, and … It's Texas at LSU. It should be a great game. Texas vs LSU: Quick Hits Texas still has to face Arkansas next before finishing up the season at Texas A&M – beating the Longhorns would be a season-maker for the Aggies. This is Senior Day for LSU. It's actually a positive that the next game is at Tennessee before finishing up the regular season at Arkansas. The two programs have only played 16 times. LSU won the last meeting 45-38 in 2019, Texas won the 2003 Cotton Bowl, and before that, the last meeting was a 13-0 LSU win in the 1963 Cotton Bowl. How To Watch Texas vs LSU Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – How many 3-loss CFP teams will there be? Why Texas Will Win Don't let LSU get into a groove. The offense is fantastic when it finds its rhythm, and moving the ball hasn't been too much of a problem in losses, compared to most normal teams, but if you can keep the Tiger ground game under wraps, everything else tends to be off. LSU threw for 380 yards against Alabama – it had to after getting down – but it only averaged 2.3 yards per carry. The Tigers were stuffed by the Mississippi State run defense, but that wasn't an issue because of the punchless Kamario Taylor-less Bulldog offense. And, not a shocker, the other bad day on the ground for LSU was in the loss to Kentucky, averaging just 2.6 yards per carry. Texas is 16th in the nation against the run, allowing just 2.9 yards per carry. Why LSU Will Win Complete your passes against Texas. The Longhorn defense might be a killer against the run, but it'll give up big plays here and there. It'll be tempting to keep cranking out the deep shots, but LSU's uptempo offense should be able to maintain some semblance of control. Sam Leavitt hasn't always been perfect, but again with the rhythm, he and the LSU attack can be devastating when the passing game clicks. Leavitt is hitting 71% of his throws this year, and even with the team's problems overall against Alabama, he has settled into his role. He hasn't been under 71% since the loss to Ole Miss back in mid-September. Texas vs LSU Prediction, Betting Lines It's a narrative I've seen coming for months. I can't shake it, and I can't back off now. Texas becomes the cause célèbre for the SEC "this three-loss team deserves to be in" faction of the college football world. It has too many good wins; the losses will be close, and dropping a tight battle in Death Valley in a Saturday night fight will be considered as acceptable as it gets. Arch Manning will have deep threat Cam Coleman to open things up, but LSU will bounce back after the problems against Alabama with its first really, really good win. And no, it won't be enough to get LSU back into the College Football Playoff discussion, but it'll be the first giant moment to set the tone for the Lane Kiffin era going forward. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) Thomas Jones · Austin American-Statesman Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads What a difference a month makes. After the Texas Longhorns dropped back-to-back games against Oklahoma and Florida , their hopes for a spot in the College Football Playoff seemed dim. But after three straight wins that include triumphs over ranked teams Ole Miss and Missouri , the No. 6 Longhorns (7-2, 4-2 SEC) enter Saturday's showdown against No. 21 LSU firmly in control of their postseason fate But Texas's first visit to Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., since 1953 looks tricky. A talented LSU squad already has three losses, and one more would all but eliminate the team from CFP contention . That's not what the rabid Tiger faithful envisioned when the program plucked head coach Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss last season and spent a small fortune on its portal payroll . Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the LSU Tigers: No. 6 Texas (7-2, 4-2 SEC) vs. No. 21 LSU (6-3, 3-3) When: 6:45 p.m. Saturday Where: Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La. TV/radio: ESPN, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: The bayou will get a little chilly Saturday, with highs only in the 50s at the kickoff and dropping down into the 40s by the final whistle. Bring a jacket, but no need for a poncho; skies should be clear and the breeze mild. Texas vs LSU football betting info Moneyline: Texas +150, LSU -180 Spread: LSU is favored by 4½ points. Over/under : 46½ points Texas history: LSU All-time: Texas leads 9-8-1 Last meeting: LSU 45, LSU 38 (Sept. 7, 2019) Most memorable meeting: LSU 45, Texas 38 (2019) By the time LSU capped its unbeaten season with a 42-25 win over Clemson in the 2019 national championship game, college football historians were already contemplating the Tigers' spot among the all-time great squads. Quarterback Joe Burrow and the Tigers produced arguably the greatest offensive season ever, and Texas fans got a taste of that firepower when Burrow threw for 471 yards and four touchdowns in a scintillating Week 2 contest at an electric Royal-Memorial Stadium. Burrow needed every yard to outduel Texas quarterback Sam Ehlinger (401 yards, five total TDs) and a Longhorn offense at the height of its powers under former coach Tom Herman . Know the foe: LSU Last week: Lost to Alabama, 31-13 Players to watch: QB Sam Leavitt , a 6-foot-2, 216-pound junior transfer from Arizona State, has thrown for 2,553 yards, 17 touchdowns and nine interceptions while completing nearly 71% of his passes and rushing for eight scores in an up-and-down season stymied by injuries. Texas fans remember him most from the 2025 Peach Bowl , when he accounted for 282 yards of offense and almost helped the Sun Devils pull off an upset in a CFP quarterfinal. WR Jackson Harris , a 6-2, 200-pound junior, looks like the next in a long lineage of game-breaking Tiger wideouts. The Hawaii transfer ranks second in the SEC with 800 yards receiving and is tied for league-high honors with seven receiving touchdowns, and he averages an impressive 17 yards a catch. LB Whit Weeks, a 6-3, 223-pound senior, looks poised to return after missing the past five games with a broken bone in his leg. An emotional leader for the Tigers, the former All-SEC player had 120 tackles in 2024 but has battled injuries over the past two seasons Central Texas connections: Senior edge Princewell Umanmielen , a former All-Centex play at Manor High School, ranks second in the SEC behind Texas's Colin Simmons with 8 ½ sacks and 12 tackles for a loss. MORE : Steve Sarkisian: CFP expansion should encourage high-profile nonconference games GOLDEN : Longhorns shows they can win a tough road game - and a whole lot more When Texas has the ball The Tigers base their defense off the ability to get to the opposing quarterback with Umanmielen, Jordan Ross (five sacks) and Deuce Geralds (five sacks). LSU ranks fourth in SEC play with 21 sacks while Texas has allowed 23 sacks in six league games, which ranks 14th in the 16-team league in sacks-per-game average. Right tackle Andre Cojoe - who replaced Trevor Goosby in the starting lineup after he suffered a knee injury three games ago - excels in the run game. But has struggled to protect quarterback Arch Manning . Texas has shown life on the ground in recent weeks behind Raleek Brown , who has 272 yards rushing over the past three games. But the Longhorns still rank just 15th in rushing in SEC play with 105.2 yards per game, and LSU excels against the run. The Tigers rank fourth in the SEC by allowing just 104 yards a game on the ground. If they can turn Texas one dimensional, they will lean on their touted pass rush to harass Manning. Texas Longhorns running back Raleek Brown (0) advances the ball, evading Missouri Tigers safety Santana Banner (15) during the game against Missouri at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium in Columbia on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) When LSU has the ball LSU racked up 457 yards in last week's 31-13 loss to Alabama and held the Tide to just 285 total yards. Two turnovers hurt, but so did the Tigers' ongoing red-zone struggles; LSU scores touchdowns in the red zone at just a 67% rate, which ranks 44th nationally. Against Alabama, the Tigers tallied just 10 points in four trips into the red zone. Texas has allowed nine touchdowns in 23 trips into the red zone by the opponent, which is the fewest in the SEC. If the Longhorns can hold LSU to field-goal tries, that could be the best indicator of an impending win. Will Simmons play for Texas? Leavitt threw a season-high 47 passes against Alabama and did tally 380 yards, but he also got sacked four times. Simmons leads the SEC in sacks despite missing two weeks and only playing 18 snaps last week against Missouri. If he's able to go Saturday, Simmons could help Texas pressure an LSU line that has only given up 17 sacks in nine games. Texas vs LSU key matchup Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles vs. LSU tight end Trey'Dez Green Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles has powered his way into the Butkus Award conversation primarily because of his 67 tackles, 10 tackles for a loss and four sacks. But the 6-1, 220-pound senior excels in pass coverage, too, as evident by his team-high six pass breakups. Towering tight end Trey'Dez Green offers a unique challenge for Biles and the Texas LBs after the 6-7 junior hauled in a career-high 10 catches for 85 yards against Alabama. Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles (3) celebrates a sack during the game against Mississippi State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs LSU prediction Thomas Jones: LSU 27, Texas 24. Death Valley dominance may be overrated; LSU is just 4-7 in home night games against higher-ranked opponents over the past decade. But desperation isn't. The Tigers need this win to stay alive in the CFP race, and Lane Kiffin pulls out all the trick to make it happen. Danny Davis: Texas. Things are back on track and UT can't afford to slip now. Look for the Louisiana Longhorns - Arch Manning on offense and Derek Williams on defense - to step up against an LSU team that has not lived up to expectations this season. Michael Shapiro: Texas 20, LSU 17: Consider this pick an effective coin flip. Both teams sport top-five defenses nationally, but the Longhorns can survive a trip to Death Valley if their offensive line repeats its inspired effort against Missouri. This game will come down to the right foot of kicker Gianni Spetic, who will deliver one of the great road wins in recent Texas history. away.headline: Whit Weeks and another injured LSU defender could return for Texas game, according to SEC report
away.blurb: Whit Weeks and another injured LSU defender could return for Texas game, according to SEC report By JON BLAU | Staff writer Jon Blau Weeks was categorized as “questionable” for the Tigers’ game against Texas in the Southeastern Conference’s initial release for the week. The senior defender has been sidelined since he suffered a lower-leg injury against Texas A&M on Sept. 26. Weeks was listed as “doubtful” on multiple SEC availability reports in the days leading up to last week’s game against Alabama. The senior was inevitably ruled out the Friday night before a 31-13 loss. LSU could also return another injured defender this Saturday, because defensive end Gabriel Reliford, who suffered an ACL tear in March during spring practice, was listed as probable for the Texas game. LSU coach Lane Kiffin previously said it was unlikely Reliford would return to play this season. Right tackle Weston Davis, who was knocked out by an injury versus Alabama, was also listed as probable for Texas. A listing of “questionable” is supposed to confer that an athlete has about a 50% chance of suiting up for that week’s game. “Doubtful” means closer to a 25% chance — and an “out” designation means a player has been ruled out completely. Aside from Weeks, LSU is without safety Dashawn Spears, receiver Phillip Wright and linebacker Charles Ross, who have all suffered season-ending injuries. But the Tigers remain relatively healthy otherwise, especially since tight end Trey’Dez Green’s return. Freshman defensive tackle Richard Anderson, who missed the Auburn and Alabama contests, was also listed as out on Wednesday’s report.
